 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R ITEM 18.1- S.L.P.(C) No. 15515/2017 & ITEM 18.2-S.L.P.(C) We have heard learned counsel for the parties.

The issue for consideration is whether the acquisition proceedings would lapse in view of Section 24(2) of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
State Of Maharashtra vs Shankar Sonu Bharambe on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191283366/
2 Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

A counter affidavit dated 22.11.2022 has been filed on behalf of all the private respondents wherein there is a clear admission of the fact in paragraphs 4 & 9 of the counter affidavit that possession of the land which was subject matter of the acquisition has been taken on 04.12.1992 and that the answering respondents are not in possession of the said land since then.
It is also admitted that award was passed in 1992 and since the compensation amount was not acceptable, the same has been deposited with the Revenue Department.

In view of the averments made in the counter affidavit referred to above and law laid down by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal reported in 2020(8) SCC 129,
the impugned judgment of the High Court does not stand the test and is liable to be set aside and is hereby set aside and the writ petitions filed before the Bombay High Court stands dismissed, the impugned order passed therein stand set aside.
It shall be open to the claimants to receive the compensation which is already lying deposited with the Revenue Department on making a proper application in that regard.
With the aforesaid, Special Leave petitions, accordingly stand allowed to that extent.
Pending application (s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

sentences.text: ITEM 18- S.L.P.(C) No. 1143/2017 & ITEM 18.3-SLP(C) No.

Learned counsel appearing for respondents-claimants at the outset states that initially the acquisition of land was made for the purpose of constructing a canal however when there was a lot of resistance by the public and farmers at large, the canal could not be constructed in continuity as a result, the State took a decision to lay down a pipeline which according to him is complete long back and land which was acquired has not at all been utilized for the same.
Learned counsel appearing for the State of Maharashtra prays for and is allowed three weeks time to seek instructions in this regard and to file an affidavit.
List after three weeks.

(SONIA GULATI) (BEENA JOLLY)
SENIOR PERSONAL ASSISTANT COURT MASTER (NSH)
